deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this folio. It is not a Riemann manuscript leaf in the mathematical sense. It is page 11 of a printed German university lecture catalogue (Verzeichniss der Vorlesungen). The professors named are Böckh, Bopp, Lachmann, J. Grimm, v. d. Hagen, Schott, Franz, Marx, Huber and others, and the catalogue mentions the Eiselen gymnastics institute, the Charité and the Ziegelstraße clinic. These details identify it as the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Berlin. The previous page cites v. d. Hagen's Nibelungenlied, 4th edition of 1842, so the catalogue dates from the mid-1840s. That fits Riemann's student years in Berlin (1847–1849), which is presumably why the sheet survives among his papers. This dating is my inference, not something the page states.

The page continues the section 'Philologische Wissenschaften und Erklärung von Schriftstellern'. It lists:
- Oriental languages: Coptic (Schwartze); Arabic (F. Benary, Wetzstein, Dieterici); Persian and Turkish (Dieterici, Pietraszewski); Chinese and Inner-Asian/Finnish literature including the Kalevala (Schott, Stuhr).
- Slavic poetry (Cybulski).
- Romance and English literature: Dante and Camões (Huber); Spanish (Franceson); Italian (Fabbrucci); English (Solly).
- A section 'Leibes-Übungen': fencing and vaulting at the Eiselen Turnanstalt, dancing (Hagemeister), riding (Fürstenberg).
- The opening of 'Öffentliche gelehrte Anstalten': library, observatory, botanical garden, museums and collections.

There are no handwritten annotations by Riemann on the page, no formulas, and no calculations. The only manuscript-like marking is the archival folio number '62' in the right margin. There is therefore nothing to reconstruct mathematically.

results.what: Printed Berlin University lecture catalogue page (philology/oriental languages, modern literatures, physical exercise, academic institutions), mid-1840s; no mathematical content
results.modern_name: Vorlesungsverzeichnis (university course catalogue) — archival/biographical context only

deep.surprise_reason: The folio is a printed course catalogue page with no mathematics and no handwritten notes. At most it is minor biographical evidence connected with Riemann's Berlin student period (1847–49), which is already well documented.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially accurate against the image.
The doubled 'von von 4-5 Uhr' (Camoens entry, top of the right column) is genuinely printed across the column break; it is not a transcription error.
The trailing '62' is the archival folio number in the right margin, not part of the printed text. The printed page number is '11' at the top.

Around the fold in the middle of the page ('Privatissime erbietet sich derselbe zu Conversationen im Arabischen, Persischen, Türkischen' and 'privatim veranstalten. Zu Privatissimis im Englischen erbietet sich derselbe'), the print is damaged and partly illegible. The transcription's readings are plausible restorations.
